matchups.recap:
Ricky Huns got their Canoeing Masters this week, surviving by 2.58 points despite Bryce Young doing his best stunned naval battle queen impression at quarterback, posting 5.42 when 17.66 was the ask. Tee Higgins carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 23.8, and Kyren Williams and Blake Corum chipped in enough that the cabin didn't need Bryce to show up at all. Thirty-eight points marinating on the bench tells you this was less a plan than a fire drill, but Boss enough wins still count.

Rome-ans 10:9-10 is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping a second straight despite Josh Jacobs, Braelon Allen, and Jaylen Warren all putting in Boss work on the ground. The real culprits wore the receiving corps: Justin Jefferson walked on the alpine vegetation with 6.4, Aaron Jones Sr. added his own puddle at 3.1, and between the two of them this cabin's passing game went soaking wet. Lone Eagle's crew had the horses but Bushwhacked without a compass at the skill positions, and that's how you lose a tug of war by less than a field goal.

Boss Section Chief ran Camp Gudge through another successful week of trail prep, leaning on Joe Burrow's 28.88 and Amon-Ra St. Brown's 19.7 to put the margin out of reach early. Kenneth Walker III and Germie Bernard both chose the Canoe Hike, and Garrett Wilson's 3.6 left him looking like a stunned naval battle queen, but it hardly mattered — Gudge still earned a post hike scrub with 89.68, their biggest margin of the entire week. I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

Campcraft Enthusiast's cabin never found its compass. Derrick Henry ate his trail cheese and salami to the tune of 5.4, while Jalen Coker and DeMario Douglas combined to get their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow — this team is gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves, because they got soaking wet across the board. At 58.06 points, Team Bradford is stuck on the Point and Back, and with a finish that low I've got to say it plain, Chief Ron Voice: "I'm disappointed in you."

Love Thy Naber ran a pig and back this week, letting CeeDee Lamb go to work for 21.9 and getting a Boss boost from Emanuel Wilson's 18.0 while Matthew Stafford quietly stacked up 17.5. Roschon Johnson chose to spend the afternoon Bushwhacking without a compass, turning a projected 8.37 into a Dutch Oven-adjacent 1.3, but the rest of the cabin had enough arrows in the bullseye that it hardly mattered. A tidy Bust Hike of a win, the kind Little Brother will take and not overthink.

Counsel's cabin, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping another one and watching the losing streak stretch out like a bad canoe trip. Baker Mayfield Stole my wow with a 6.66 outing nobody asked for, A.J. Brown turned 13.37 projected into 6.3 actual, and Denzel Boston's 4.2 had the whole cabin Walking on the alpine vegetation. Luther Burden III's 21.7 and a Swift-Gibbs combo kept the scoreboard respectable, but respectable doesn't win Tuna Casserole.

Chef Boyardee ran the Goose is Loose through another camp activity with a plan that had holes you could paddle a canoe through. Dak Prescott did his part at 23.28 and Jonathan Taylor chipped in 18.0, but Tetairoa McMillan walked on the alpine vegetation all afternoon, posting 6.0 against a projection more than double that. Coach Steffanowitz can talk about the preparation all he wants, but a cabin that gets this little from its supporting cast looked like a Woodsman playing Chief Tyler Hallenbeck in Tetherball by the end of the counselor's ledger, final margin notwithstanding.

Funk that Junk, meanwhile, had Drake Maye and Jaxon Smith-Njigba carrying the load like Woodsman Chiefs on a hike, 27.44 and 26.8 respectively, with Bucky Irving tagging along for 23.5. Yes, Nico Collins stole the wow with 1.6 points and Ted Hurst III turned in a full Dutch Oven, but Old Balls had banked enough elsewhere to coast. A 23.46-point win and a well-earned Tuna Casserole for the Funk cabin tonight — the Goose, meanwhile, heads back to the bunk still bushwhacking without a compass.

The Machine Knows squeaked out a Canoeing Masters this week, 119.72 to 118.32, the kind of margin that has the whole lineup sweating through the flag-raising. Javonte Williams carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 21.5, Tre Tucker and Puka Nacua chipped in boss yardage of their own, and that was enough cushion to survive Matthew Golden's 6.9 and Sam LaPorta's stunned naval battle queen impression at tight end. The counselor drew it tight but the plan held.

Harley Jarvis had every reason to stroll off with the Tuna Casserole after Tony Pollard's absurd 35-point hike and Zay Flowers' 23.7, but Kendre Miller and Isaiah Likely had their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow right when Blue Ridge needed steadiness, combining for barely more than a canteen's worth of points. A matchup this close always comes down to the quiet collapses, and this week it was the depth chart beyond the headliners that cost Harley Jarvis a win that was sitting right there on the trail.

home.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Canoeing Masters is the right description for this one, as Catalina Wine Mixon scraped by with a 92.9 to 91.52 nail-biter that felt more like a tug of war decided by inches than a decisive camp activity. Trey McBride and Rhamondre Stevenson carried the load like Woodsman Chiefs on a hike, posting 22.1 and 20.0 to drag the Chair Force across the finish line even while Patrick Mahomes turned in a stunned naval battle queen performance at 6.0 and Xavier Worthy went fishing for his trail mix instead of targets, managing only 2.6. The plan survived its own mistakes, barely.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare is stuck on the Point and Back after dropping another squeaker, now Stuck in the Sewards for consecutive weeks despite Christian McCaffrey's respectable 19.0 and Drake London's 16.1. The counselor's preparation left this cabin a single point short of sticky buns on Sunday morning, proof that close only counts in horseshoes and canoe races, not camp standings.

headline: Week 7 delivers one blowout and five nail-biters
